A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Nous framework despite the changed title. All pages, equations, tables, figures, and appendices were readable, allowing retained, relocated, and revised content to be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original diagram-generation experiments, training and reward ablations, human-user evaluations, and collaborative novel-writing results.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and reports expanded human testing and additional comparisons with UoT and CQ-Gen.

M1.justification: The structured belief state, hard-constraint updates, entropy-reduction reward, and offline GRPO optimization remain unchanged. Renaming the 'world model' to 'empirical prior' and explaining unweighted entropy do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: V2 adds an evaluated draft-start scenario in which users supply partial initial information, alongside starting from scratch. Scientific diagram generation and collaborative novel writing remain the same covered domains.

E2.justification: New Appendix A/Table 5 evaluates UoT and CQ-Gen against Nous under zero-start and draft-start conditions. This substantially extends comparison beyond the retained training variants and Socratic prompting baselines. Only dialogue turns and information gain are compared for these new methods.

E3.justification: Human evaluation changes from three doctoral students to ten participants with zero-start and draft-start conditions; v2 reports 2,000 interaction logs. The new UoT comparison uses sparse sampling with N=5. Appendix D also changes the reported VisPainter designer from Gemini-2.5-Pro to Gemini-1.5-Pro, without establishing whether the retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: The user-adaptability analysis extends to partial initial drafts and discusses variation across ten participants. The entropy-versus-counting ablation and the Template/Vague/Noisy training-data robustness experiment remain unchanged.

E5.justification: New Appendix F reports uncertainty-style quantities for human results, including 17.3±2.5 zero-start turns and 7.6±1.8 draft-start turns. It does not define what the ± values represent or provide a significance test. Existing Table 2 confidence-bound reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 4 revises oracle win rates and replaces the earlier human result of 18.7 turns/128.01 IG with zero-start results of 17.3/126.44 and draft-start results of 7.6/42.31. New Table 5 adds UoT and CQ-Gen results, including zero-start IG of 38.38 and 9.72. These are added or replaced findings under revised settings; Tables 1–3 and the existing noise-ablation and novel-writing results remain numerically identical.

T1.justification: The formal specification space, independence assumption, entropy derivation, and optimization equations are retained. Equation 6 is shortened equivalently. New discussion of implicit weighting and independence-related inefficiency supplies interpretation rather than a new proof or formal result.

C1.justification: V1's abstract and introduction describe the framework as domain-agnostic with demonstrated generalization. V2 removes that abstract claim and presents the additional domain experiment as suggesting generalization potential. The central contributions concerning Nous, information-gain rewards, and automated training data remain.

C2.justification: Appendices C–E substantially expand applicability boundaries, emphasizing structural constraints and a significant intention gap. They discuss diminishing returns from strong narrative priors, entropy overestimation and redundant questions under independence, and rendering-complexity tradeoffs. V2 also removes v1's explicit simulation limitation concerning changing goals, frustration, and evolving human behavior.

D1.justification: V2 documents participant qualifications, task counts, reference-image instructions, and unrestricted language use, and specifies UoT's N=5 sampling. Training hardware, hyperparameters, prompt templates, and statements about accompanying code attachments remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A substantially expand positioning against traditional slot-filling dialogue and explain claimed limitations of UoT planning and CQ-Gen clarification. V2 adds MultiWOZ-related and conditional-independence literature while removing the standalone AI-for-design discussion. These changes extend substantive comparison with prior research beyond bibliographic corrections.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, affiliations and contact information, replaces 'world model' with 'empirical prior,' and revises selected introductory and appendix passages. It adds a user-testing appendix while retaining most method exposition and the overall section sequence.

P2.justification: V2 reformats the main text and references into two columns, adds the conceptual Figure 1, redraws the pipeline figure, expands Table 4, and adds Table 5. The unchanged win-rate heatmaps move from the main text to Appendix J, and existing example figures are repositioned and enlarged.

improvement.justification: The expanded human study and direct UoT/CQ-Gen comparisons strengthen evidence beyond v1's small human evaluation and prompt/training baselines. Narrower generalization claims and explicit applicability boundaries improve calibration. These gains are limited by undefined uncertainty values, Figure 4(c) retaining superseded human results, and the unexplained designer-version change despite unchanged scores. Removing the earlier caveat about evolving human goals also weakens the limitations discussion.
